messages:
joanna_sales: Need an enterprise POC hosted key for NovaHealth next week. They insist on IP allowlist + auditable rotation proof. Can we do a short-lived key and provide a rotation/revoke export they can include in their compliance pack?

marc_se: Yes. For enterprise demos I usually issue a scoped key with ttl=48h and an IP allowlist. That gives a clear audit trail and low blast radius.

marc_se: If they want rotation proof, we can do overlapping rotation: create new key ~2h before expiry, flip clients, then revoke old key. Each action is logged with actor and timestamp.

joanna_sales: How to create the key (I need a copy-paste snippet for the onboarding doc)?

rachel_infra: Use the service account from sales-ops. Example POST payload (JSON body):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SA_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"name":"nova-poc-enterprise","scopes":["generate:text","embeddings:read"],"ttl_seconds":172800,"ip_allowlist":["198.51.100.0/24","203.0.113.45/32"],"notes":"POC for NovaHealth - enterprise"}' | jq .
```

rachel_infra: We return key metadata including key_id (kr_200001). The plaintext token is shown once. Save to vault.

pete_security: Security checklist: require 2FA on SA that requests the key, record justification in ticket, and set TTL <= 7 days. For NovaHealth I'd also set SSO restriction on who can view the token in the console.

joanna_sales: What about mobile demo clients? They will show a mobile app in the demo. IP allowlist might break that.

marc_se: For mobile, route requests through a short-lived backend session broker. Mobile talks to your backend over TLS; backend exchanges a server-side short-lived key (not the main SA) for calls to Redwood. That keeps keys off-device.

rachel_infra: Rotation flow we recommend: 1) Create kr_new, 2) deploy to demo backend, 3) smoke test, 4) revoke kr_old. Never rotate in-place.

joanna_sales: Revocation command for docs?

rachel_infra: Revoke API (POST) and Console revoke both create audit events. Example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/kr_200001/revoke \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SA_TOKEN'
```
Or DELETE if using internal tooling:
```bash
# internal-only
DELETE /v1/internal/keys/kr_200001
```

pete_security: Audit export: infra can export events for key_id in JSON with a time range. Endpoint: GET /v1/audit/events?key_id=kr_200001&from=2112340000&to=2112400000. We can sign that export and attach it to the compliance packet.

ops-bot: [automated] key_request: id=kr_200001 owner=joanna_sales ttl=172800 scope=generate:text,embeddings:read ip_allowlist=[198.51.100.0/24] status=pending-approval

rachel_infra: Approving now. Note on log retention: default POC retention is 90 days; enterprise can request 365d retention for audit exports—ticket needed.

marc_se: If the POC later needs sustained throughput, we create a small Dedicated pool and issue a separate key scoped to that pool. That keeps billing/tracking clean.

joanna_sales: Perfect. Please add the curl snippets and the audit-export example into the onboarding doc and link the signed export once available. Leaving thread open for the compliance packet link.
